old_caption: The video captures a first-person perspective of a person in a whitewater environment, viewed from behind. The individual wears a helmet with a mounted camera and a life vest, facing turbulent, foamy water flowing between large rocks. In the background, a crowd of spectators sits and stands on rocks along the riverbank, observing. Several other people in outdoor gear are visible near the water, including one in a yellow suit standing on a rock above the current and another in a green jacket standing in the water. The surrounding area is a forest with trees showing autumn colors. The camera remains relatively steady, capturing the dynamic movement of the water and the static presence of the onlookers and other participants. The overall atmosphere is one of active engagement with a natural, rugged setting.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures an exhilarating scene of whitewater rafting on a rocky river. The camera, positioned at the front of the raft, provides a first-person perspective, immersing the viewer in the action. The raft navigates through turbulent waters, splashing against the rocks and creating white foam. In the background, a group of spectators stands on the riverbank, watching intently. Some individuals in the crowd are dressed in outdoor gear, suggesting they are also participants or enthusiasts. The surrounding landscape is lush with trees, some of which have autumn foliage, indicating the season. The riverbanks are rugged and uneven, adding to the challenge of the rafting experience. The camera remains steady throughout, capturing the dynamic movement of the water and the raft's journey down the river. The overall atmosphere is one of excitement and adventure, with the natural beauty of the environment providing a stunning backdrop to the thrilling activity.
caption: The video captures an over-the-shoulder view from behind a paddler's helmet in turbulent whitewater. The back of the paddler's green-and-black helmet, topped with a small action camera, and the yellow vest over teal sleeves fill the lower foreground. Ahead, white water boils and churns continuously between large grey boulders. A person in a green top and yellow helmet stands on a midstream rock facing the paddler, while farther back a figure in yellow perches atop a boulder, staying in place. On the right bank, a crowd of spectators sits and stands on the rocks, watching. The background is an autumn forest of bare trunks and brown-orange foliage under an overcast sky. The viewpoint shifts subtly, the left boulder and foreground leaves changing position slightly. A greyish spray plume above the central boulder grows more defined and then persists as a standing veil of mist. The turbulent whitewater motion is already underway and continues.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
